rule: identities are resolved against EXISTING Atlas ids by GUI evidence; no id is created; duplicates are reported, not merged

resolutions.basis: GUI tooltip 'A Uni Blend (75)/(30)' tracks the raw value; default 75 matches the state-readback default
resolutions.open: the Atlas holds TWO ids for this control (oscA.blend from the UI inventory, oscA.detune_width from the schema); the registry must merge them -- not done here

resolutions.basis: raw -50 shows as WIDTH -50 in the UNISON settings panel; 'Uni Width' (UI inventory) and 'Unison Stereo Width' (schema, -100..100, default 100) are the same control
resolutions.open: duplicate Atlas ids; the panel's other fields (MODE, STACK, RANGE, WT POS, WARP 1/2) have their own raw keys not yet mapped

resolutions.basis: tooltip 'A WT Pos'; raw 128 displays as frame 5
resolutions.open: the display is table-dependent (frame index): 0..256 is the RAW domain only

resolutions.basis: tooltip 'A Warp (50 %)' for raw 0.5; also upstream mapping.py warp_amount -> kParamWarp
raw value shows in the OSC A phase readout (degrees); default displays 180
resolutions.open: Atlas default says 0; observed default is 180

resolutions.basis: CRS box tracks the raw value; tooltip 'A Coarse Pitch (64.00)'
resolutions.open: the Atlas note said the CRS <-> kParamCoarsePit relation was not established: it is now (two Atlas ids, one control)

resolutions.basis: raw 0.0 turns the module bypass icon red (Atlas: blue=active, red=bypassed)
resolutions.open: a per-module-INSTANCE control (fx_chain index), not one global scalar

resolutions.basis: raw 0.9 moves the module's right-edge output LEVEL fader
resolutions.open: the Atlas entry says 'no separate Level control, confirmed absent' and flags a retest: the control exists (a fader, not a knob), so that entry needs correcting; only visual evidence, no numeric readout
